chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Umar from Ibn Mahbub from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
When it is the Day of Judgment, a caller will call out: 'Where are those who were hostile to my lovers?' Then a group of people will stand up whose faces will have no flesh.
It will be said: 'These are the people who hurt the believers, set themselves against them, were stubborn with them, and humiliated them because of their religion.'
He said: Then they will be ordered to be taken to Hell.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I swear by Allah! These are the people who used to agree with the words of believers, but they withheld their rights and exposed their secrets.'

key_terms.الصُّدُود: The hostile ones / those who turned away

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'hostile ones' (al-Sudood) mentioned in the hadith regarding the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describing the Day of Judgment where a caller identifies 'al-Sudud' (the hostile ones) against God's lovers, whose faces are stripped of flesh as a sign of their affliction. These individuals are condemned not merely for open opposition, but for the subtle betrayal of withholding rights and exposing secrets while outwardly feigning agreement. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the spiritual and social harms of hypocrisy and enmity towards the faithful, leading to their specific summons to Hell.
